scientific_queries.note: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage at the drug level, to test whether borrowing strength makes the pathway prior usable.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round closes the mechanism chain and its own gate turns out to add an unnecessary conjunct.

the_primary_question_answered_yes.question: does shrinkage make the pathway prior beat an uninformed baseline
the_primary_question_answered_yes.evidence: shrunk minus grand is significantly positive on both (+0.0000756) and anchor (+0.000099)
the_primary_question_answered_yes.flip: on the library side R2 goes from -0.1531 with the crude estimator to +0.0667 with shrinkage

my_gate_was_wrong_again.what_i_required: both a win over the grand mean AND a win over the crude estimator
my_gate_was_wrong_again.why_the_second_conjunct_is_wrong: the question is whether shrinkage makes the prior usable, which is the comparison against an uninformed baseline; beating crude is a separate and stricter demand, and on the pooled side there is little room because crude already reaches R2 0.151
my_gate_was_wrong_again.count: fifth instance of the same family, after R103, R107, R112 and R142

prior_strength.reading: about 28 percent of drug-level variance in mean response lies between pathways; this is the quantity the annotation is worth, and it explains why five drugs per group require borrowing strength

the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.1: pathway membership is associated with drug behaviour (C110)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.2: a crude group mean cannot exploit it (C110)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.4: at the model level ridge performs exactly that shrinkage (C106)
the_mechanism_chain_is_closed.so: the prior is real, exploitable only with borrowing of strength, and the regularised model does the borrowing automatically

limits: moments rather than REML, and truncating tau-squared at zero affects lambda
the library-side comparison against the grand mean is only marginal
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: the mechanism line is complete; linking prior strength to substitution magnitude would need a second resource with a different tau-squared

register_updates.C111: new: shrinkage makes the prior usable and closes the chain
